periods.time: vol-17 ch-006, two weeks before the narration's present framing
periods.summary: The epilogue explains that Or-Gaule's destruction of Rebellion collapses the old balance among the International Mage-Knight League, the Great Powers/Union, and Rebellion, pushing the League and Union toward direct conflict. At the ruined Rebellion headquarters in the Alps, three armed helicopters deploy American PSYON troops. Rinna, Charlotte and Sara prepare to defend Kozo Kazamatsuri and Japanese Prime Minister Bakuya Tsukikage, but Kozo orders them to stand down because Abraham Carter, PSYON's captain and America's strongest psychic, has arrived. Abraham descends without a parachute, lands before Kozo and Tsukikage, identifies them, and asks on behalf of the United States and world justice whether they are enemies or allies and which side they belong to.
periods.cause: Rebellion's destruction removes the buffer between global powers, and Tsukikage and Kozo are found at Rebellion's ruined headquarters during the ensuing scramble.
periods.outcome: A direct American demand for allegiance is issued; the answer is left unresolved.
periods.significance: Sets up the post-Vermillion arc's world-order conflict and marks the beginning of open League-Union confrontation after Rebellion's fall.
